channel.title: NPR Programs: Morning Edition
channel.description: Morning Edition takes listeners around the country and the world with multi-faceted stories and commentaries every weekday. Hosts Steve Inskeep, Leila Fadel, Michel Martin and A Martínez bring you the latest breaking news and features to prepare you for the day.

item.title: After midterm losses, Trump makes changes to his inner circle
item.description: President Trump is shaking up his closest advisers after Democrats made huge gains in the midterm elections.
item.content:encoded: President Trump is shaking up his closest advisers after Democrats made huge gains in the midterm elections.

item.title: Trump appoints Stephen Miller as his new chief of staff
item.description: The president selected Stephen Miller as his new chief of staff. NPR's Leila Fadel speaks with Miles Taylor, a former Department of Homeland Security chief of staff who worked with Miller.

item.title: U.N. climate talks begin today. Here are 3 things to know
item.description: Countries are gathering in Antalya, Turkey, for the annual U.N. climate conference. Many are frustrated with the lack of focus on fossil fuels, the main driver of climate change.

item.title: Supreme Court weighs effort to shield federal law enforcement as ICE complaints rise
item.description: The Supreme Court considers the case of a prisoner who suffered brutal injuries, only to be denied medical care behind bars. He wants to sue the prison nurse in a case that could change the law on holding federal officers accountable.

item.title: Congress is coming back to Washington. Here's what to expect
item.description: Lawmakers are coming back to Washington this week after the midterm elections. Republicans plan to finish work on several outstanding issues before Democrats take control of Congress in January.

item.title: Palantir hires a former Democratic senator as it faces scrutiny in new Congress
item.description: The secretive software company has been accused of letting its powerful tools be used by the Trump administration to surveil Americans. Now it's hiring former Sen. Jon Tester to burnish its image.

item.title: In 'Gentle Monster,' a pervert's normality is the horrifying factor
item.description: NPR's Leila Fadel speaks with Léa Seydoux about her new film Gentle Monster, in which she plays a concert pianist whose life falls apart after her husband is accused of a crime.

item.title: Israel's president taps Netanyahu's political rival to form a new government
item.description: Israel's president has tapped Benjamin Netanyahu's chief political rival, Gadi Eisenkot, to form a new government following an inconclusive election that left the country's leadership in limbo.

item.title: Midterm results could complicate JD Vance's political future
item.description: Vice President JD Vance is looking to recast his political fortune after serving as the Trump administration's No. 2 while his party suffered a historic wipeout.
